newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul allows 2.46 trln won corporate issues in May.
newsitem.headline: Seoul allows 2.46 trln won corporate issues in May.

text.p: The Korea Securities Dealers Association said on Wednesday it had approved plans by domestic companies to issue a combined 2.46 trillion won of three-year corporate bonds in May.
The amount compared to 2.45 trillion won worth of the bonds approved for issue in April, the government-controlled association said in a statement.
It said 56 percent, or 1.38 trillion won, of the total approved for May was aimed at raising operating funds, compared with 1.37 trillion won in April.
The next biggest amount of 666.65 billion won, or 27.1 percent of the total, was for raising funds to pay back bonds due to mature during May, it said.
The remaining amount of 417 billion won was for facility investment, it added.
